title: Canonical affine-line duality over arbitrary affine bases
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring, let $N\geq1$ satisfy $NA=0$, let $S$ be any affine scheme on which $N$ is invertible, and let $p:\mathbf A^1_S\to S$ be the affine-line projection [def-sbc-affine-space]. Use the ordinary unbounded etale categories, compact-support adjoint $G_p$, $\omega_p=G_pA_S$ and $\theta_p$ of [lem-sf-etale-ambient-adjoint-projection], with the standard open-then-proper factorization $\mathbf A^1_S\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^1_S\to S$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. Put $T=A_{\mathbf A^1_S}(1)=\mu_{N,\mathbf A^1_S}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/N}A_{\mathbf A^1_S}$, with its roots-of-unity action and constant coefficients as in [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line]. There exists an isomorphism $\gamma_p:T[2]\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_p$ such that, for every $K\in D(S_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, the actual composite
$$T[2]\otimes_A^Lp^*K\xrightarrow{\gamma_p\otimes1}\omega_p\otimes_A^Lp^*K\xrightarrow{\theta_{p,K}}G_pK$$
is an isomorphism. There is no Noetherian, constructibility, boundedness or Tor-amplitude hypothesis on $S$ or $K$.

source.place: Paragraphs 2-3, the affine-line building block of the affine-space adjunction and its counit-defined tensor mate; the arbitrary-affine-base input AffineLineSmoothDuality is stated in upstream SmoothDuality/AffineSpace.lean lines 125-136. Generalizes the Noetherian cor-amb-affine-space-adjunction only in dimension one; no general smooth theorem is asserted.

proof.text: Write $X=\mathbf A^1_S$, $P=\mathbf P^1_S$, and $p=qj$ for the standard chart $j:X\hookrightarrow P$. The chart is an open immersion over $S$ by [lemma-nagata-relative-affine-space-open-immersion], and $q$ is proper by [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper]. Supply $q$ with $(\mathrm{id}_P,q)$, $j$ with $(j,\mathrm{id}_P)$, and $p$ with $(j,q)$. These are precisely the factorizations used below. In particular $F_q=Rq_*$ and $F_p=Rq_*Dj_!$ by [lem-sf-etale-ambient-adjoint-projection]. Set $B=A_P(1)[2]$. Invertibility of $N$ on $P$ follows by applying its structure-sheaf ring maps to a local inverse on $S$.

Apply [lem-sf-affine-base-p1-trace-adjunction] to $S,A,N$, obtaining $F_q\dashv H$ with $HK=B\otimes_A^Lq^*K$ and trace $t:F_qB\to A_S$. The ambient adjunction is $F_q\dashv G_q$ [lem-sf-etale-ambient-adjoint-projection]. By [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint] there is a counit-preserving natural isomorphism $e:H\xrightarrow{\sim}G_q$, satisfying $\epsilon^G_K\circ F_q(e_K)=\epsilon^H_K$. Let $r:B\xrightarrow{\sim}H(A_S)$ be the inverse right unitor, with $q^*A_S=A_P$ inserted, and put $\gamma_q=e_{A_S}\circ r:B\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_q$. The counit equation at $A_S$ gives $\epsilon^G_{A_S}\circ F_q(\gamma_q)=t$. In the Lean proof choose the projective right adjoint to be H itself, with the trace adjunction; no separate chosen ambient projective adjoint is needed. The proof-only helper tensorMap_of_trace_adjunction performs the counit-preserving comparison for any selected adjoint, using projection naturality, the trace formula and the explicit unit equation.

source.place: Construct the projection-normalized projective adjunction, then identify its right adjoint

proof.text:
For arbitrary $K$, transpose $\theta_{q,K}\circ(\gamma_q\otimes1)$ under $F_q\dashv G_q$. By the definition of $\theta$ and naturality of its projection isomorphism, its transpose is
$$\lambda_K\circ(\epsilon^G_{A_S}\otimes1)\circ\mathrm{PF}_{\omega_q,K}^{-1}\circ F_q(\gamma_q\otimes1)
=\lambda_K\circ((\epsilon^G_{A_S}\circ F_q\gamma_q)\otimes1)\circ\mathrm{PF}_{B,K}^{-1}
=\lambda_K\circ(t\otimes1)\circ\mathrm{PF}_{B,K}^{-1}=\epsilon^H_K.$$
The last equality is exactly the counit formula in [lem-sf-affine-base-p1-trace-adjunction]. Step 2 says $e_K$ has this same transpose. Injectivity of the adjunction bijection therefore gives $\theta_{q,K}\circ(\gamma_q\otimes1)=e_K$. Both $e_K$ and $\gamma_q\otimes1$ are isomorphisms, so every $\theta_{q,K}$ is an isomorphism. This is a direct substitution of the two counit formulas; it uses no unproved compatibility of unrelated isomorphisms. The calculation is proved first in the abstract private helper tensorMap_of_trace, then instantiated by tensorMap_of_trace_adjunction; this avoids unfolding geometric derived-category constructions throughout the formal calculation.

source.place: Paragraph 3: transpose the actual tensor map and compare counits

proof.text:
The open immersion $j$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale] and separated: its monomorphism property makes its diagonal the identity of $X$, a closed immersion. The factorizations in step 1 allow [lem-sf-etale-unit-tensor-arbitrary-base] to identify $G_j$ with $j^*$ and make its tensor maps invertible. Apply the etale restriction clause of [lem-sf-exceptional-tensor-transitivity] to $a=j$, $b=q$, $h=p$. Its counit-preserving comparison $\lambda_K:j^*G_qK\xrightarrow{\sim}G_pK$ obeys
$$\lambda_K\circ j^*\theta_{q,K}=\theta_{p,K}\circ(\lambda_{A_S}\otimes1),$$
with its specified tensor/pullback identifications. Since $\theta_{q,K}$ is invertible by step 3 and both $\lambda$ components are invertible, this equation makes $\theta_{p,K}$ invertible for every unbounded $K$. No tensor-invertibility hypothesis is needed for this etale restriction clause. The private helper tensorMap_etale_restriction applies exactly sfExceptionalTensorEtaleRestriction, then cancels its three invertible leading factors. It constructs the etale right adjoint using the ambient existence theorem; uniqueness of right adjoints determines this data up to natural isomorphism.

source.place: Paragraphs 2-3: etale restriction with equality of canonical tensor maps

proof.text:
The canonical roots-of-unity pullback of [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] identifies $j^*B$ with $A_X(1)[2]=T[2]$, including its $\mathbf Z/N$ action and coefficient extension. Define
$$\gamma_p:T[2]\xrightarrow{\sim}j^*B\xrightarrow{j^*\gamma_q}j^*\omega_q\xrightarrow{\lambda_{A_S}}\omega_p.$$
All three arrows are isomorphisms. By step 4 the second arrow in the composite asked for in the statement is $\theta_{p,K}$ and is invertible. Its first arrow is tensoring the isomorphism $\gamma_p$ with $1_{p^*K}$, hence is invertible. Their composite is therefore invertible. This proves the requested assertion for the actual $\theta_p$, with no restriction on $K$. In Lean finiteEtaleTwistPullbackData.c at exponent one is placed in degree zero, composed with singleFunctorCompLeftDerivedUpperStarIso and the pullback commShiftIso. Stalkwise invertibility on S maps to the projective stalks, hence to its global sections, and then to the affine-chart global sections.
